subject: Film & Cinema
title: D.W. Griffith and the Feature Film
description: A quick win: understand D.W. Griffith and the Feature Film.

hook.text: Before 1915, most films lasted only ten to fifteen minutes.

buildup.text: D.W. Griffith directed The Birth of a Nation — over three hours of epic storytelling.

discovery.text: He pioneered close-ups, cross-cutting, and fade-outs that became standard grammar.

twist.text: The film's racist content makes it one of cinema's most controversial milestones.

climax.text: Griffith proved movies could be as ambitious as novels or operas.

punchline.text: He invented film language, then misused it.

quiz.question: What did D.W. Griffith pioneer in filmmaking?
options: Close-ups, cross-cutting, and other editing techniques
